name: Integer Underflow (Wrap or Wraparound)
principle: A subtraction produces a value below the type's minimum and wraps or otherwise becomes incorrect. If that wrapped value is then used as a size, index, offset, or counter, it can corrupt data, crash the program, or create exploitable control flow.
detection_signals: `x = a - b` where `a` or `b` comes from input, packet length, or external state
`size_t`/unsigned destination assigned from subtraction of signed or mixed-sign operands
`--i` or `i--` on an unsigned loop counter with termination logic depending on `i >= 0` or similar
`len = total_len - header_len` without a preceding `header_len <= total_len` check
subtraction result passed to `malloc()`, `new[]`, stack array size, `memcpy()`, `memmove()`, `read()`, or `write()`
subtraction used as array index, slice length, or bounds check input after mixed signed/unsigned conversion
negative_signals: explicit precheck `if (a < b) return error;` before `a - b`
checked arithmetic such as `__builtin_sub_overflow(a, b, &out)` with error handling
C# `checked { x = a - b; }` with overflow handling
descending loop pattern `for (size_t i = n; i-- > 0; )` or equivalent non-underflowing form
subtraction of compile-time constants that cannot reach the type minimum
false_defense_traps: using unsigned types for both operands; unsigned subtraction still wraps
casting the wrapped result to a wider type after subtraction
clamping or `abs()` after the subtraction instead of checking before it
checking only an upper bound on the result after wraparound
assuming `size_t` prevents underflow because it is non-negative
verification_focus: Can this subtraction ever go below the type's minimum before the result is used as a length, index, offset, or loop counter?

consequence_chains.trigger: wrapped subtraction is used to compute allocation or buffer size
consequence_chains.consequence: wrong-sized allocation or stack array size can lead to crash or later overflow

consequence_chains.trigger: wrapped subtraction feeds a copy length or array index
unsigned loop counter underflows in loop termination logic
consequence_chains.consequence: infinite loop and denial of service

patch_principle: use checked subtraction APIs or compiler overflow intrinsics
validate external length and offset fields before arithmetic
promote to a wider type only if the wider range is also bounded and checked
fail closed on underflow instead of wrapping or truncating the result

minimal_examples.safe: if (header_len > total_len) return error; size_t len = total_len - header_len;
